turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey, nice to hear from you. How are you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, a little stressed, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm autistic and I find eye contact and small talk in interviews really draining. Can I ask for changes?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, you can ask for reasonable adjustments. Many employers are used to it and will happily help.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, and another thing. My book club wants to try a new format and I have to suggest one tonight.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've narrowed it down to a few. You'll hear them all, then I'll ask you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We could all read different books on the same theme and then swap recommendations.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Another idea is picking one very short book and reading it right there at the meeting.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or we pick a book that was turned into a film, read it, and then watch the film together.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, um, that's everything, I think. Your thoughts?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The film night is the easiest sell, since people get a reward for finishing. Reading a short book at the meeting is cozy but might feel like school. The theme idea is great for variety but discussions can get scattered.
